messages:
alex_g: Quick heads up — HealthCo is pushing for exported audit bundles to include a proof-of-possession (PoP) for KMS-wrapped keys plus an event-level signature they can validate. Legal says this will be an acceptance criterion in the contract/SLA. Any immediate red flags?

mina: We currently attach a bundle signature on exports but we don't produce a PoP attestation from customer KMSes. Need to clarify: do they want confirmation the bundle was wrapped with their KMS key, or a separate attestation token from the KMS?

samir: From the customer call it sounded like both: they want a detached signature for the bundle (non-repudiable) and an attestation token proving the wrapping key existed and was used at sign time. Typical FedRAMP-style ask.

jen_legal: For contracts: proposed acceptance criteria draft — 1) bundle verifies against a cert/JWKS provided by Redwood; 2) each exported bundle contains a "kms_attestation" blob with nonce+timestamp; 3) Redwood provides verification instructions and a 30-day acceptance test window. We'll need an addendum if this increases data handling obligations.

alex_g: Implementation thoughts: we can keep the detached signature (e.g., PKCS7 or an RFC7468-like detached sig) and include key metadata (kid, alg). For PoP we can surface a KMS attestation blob in the bundle when customer configures "export_with_attestation:true" on their tenant. For HSM-backed customer KMS (external), we can accept their attestation blob and include it in the archive. For cloud KMS we might call the provider's attestation API if available, or require the customer to provide the attestation token.

mina: Example of a minimal bundle.json shape I mocked up: ```json
{
  "events": [ { "ts":"2025-03-15T18:40:01Z", "type":"api_key.rotate", "actor":"system" } ],
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG==",
  "signature_kid": "redwood-export-signing-v1",
  "kms_attestation": {
    "provider":"aws-kms",
    "attestation_blob":"BASE64_ATTEST==",
    "key_id":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-1234",
    "timestamp":"2025-03-15T18:42:00Z"
  }
}```

samir: A few implementation risks to call out: key rotation/revocation (how does customer verify old bundles after key rotation?), long-term verifiability (if returning to bundle after months/years), and attestation replay protection (we should require nonce+timestamp and include the nonce in the signature scope). We should include the signing cert chain or a JWKS url inside the bundle (or both).

ops-bot: :warning: Note: any changes that expand exported data or retention could affect compliance controls. Please file a change request and update the export runbook.

jen_legal: Contract-level asks: propose an SLA / acceptance checklist: (A) Delivery of signed bundle and attestation; (B) Customer can run provided verification script within 30 days; (C) Redwood provides statement of verification steps and maintains signing key history for 1 year for forensic validation; (D) Liability cap and indemnity language to be added for PoP guarantees.

alex_g: Action items: 1) Mina to open a draft schema PR for audit bundle + example verification script; 2) Samir to write threat model and verification checklist (nonce handling, timestamp skew, replay); 3) Jen to draft contract addendum language and acceptance test definition; 4) Solutions/SE to schedule hands-on acceptance run with HealthCo.

mina: I'll open the PR tonight. Sample verification workflow I'll include in the repo: verify signature -> validate attestation blob with provider-specific verification -> check nonce/timestamp.

samir: Also add a section "expired_key_verification" explaining how to validate bundles signed by rotated keys (include archived JWKS/certs in the bundle or point to an auditable key history endpoint).

alex_g: Great. Can we aim to have a v0 bundle + verification script for the customer demo next week? :thumbsup:

mina: Yes, aiming for v0 by EOD Friday.

jen_legal: I'll prep the addendum draft and ping legal reviewers.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Change request created: CR-2025-114 (export-audit-attestation). Please link PR when ready.
